title: Policy Weave: Automated Reconciliation for Residency & Retention Policies
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated reconciliation service (Policy Weave) that continuously asserts that tenant-level data residency and data retention settings match the canonical policy-as-code declarations, and that it can automatically remediate safe, low-risk mismatches while generating tamper-evident evidence bundles for audits. This reduces manual cloud audits, prevents silent configuration drift, and creates a single source of truth for residency/retention enforcement across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope:
- Authoritative policy model for residency (region locks, sovereign buckets) and retention (TTL per artifact type).
- Continuous comparator that samples live config, compares to policy-as-code, and assigns risk-levels.
- Automated remediation engine for safe actions (tagging, policy re-attach, TTL patch) with an approval step for high-risk changes.
- Evidence generator that snapshots before/after state, signs the bundle, and uploads to the compliance S3 bucket and console.
- Integration points: Infra Config API, Tenant Config Service, Console audit API, Observability metrics, and the Compliance Orchestrator.

Out of scope: historic manual audits, encryption key rotation, and cross-tenant policy migration.
technical_notes:
Architecture: lightweight Kubernetes cron-controller + controller loop that performs policy evaluation using the Policy Weave engine (policy-as-code DSL compiled to evaluation graphs). Evaluation uses the same language as the Compliance Orchestrator to avoid dual-definition.

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Frequency vs. load: default evaluation window is 15m per high-risk tenant shard; lower-risk tenants evaluated every 6h. We snapshot config via the Tenant Config Service rather than querying cloud APIs directly to reduce rate limits.
- Remediation safety: only apply automatic fixes for no-op or idempotent ops (e.g., re-attaching shielded policy, setting TTL to a larger retention ceiling). For deletion/shortening TTLs or region moves, create an auto-created remediation request and trigger approval workflow in Console.
- Evidence size: compress and sign bundles; keep pointers in audit store and purge old bundles after retention policy for evidence.

Data model: flattened key/value list per resource to satisfy agents.md requirement for simple shapes in telemetry.
implementation_plan:
1) Design policy mapping and canonical schema (2 days)
2) Implement evaluator service and unit tests (5 days)
3) Build comparator that diff's tenant config vs policy (3 days)
4) Implement safe remediation primitives and approval hooks (4 days)
5) Evidence bundler and signer + upload flow (3 days)
6) Integrate with Console for alerts and runbook links (2 days)
7) End-to-end QA and staged rollout (5 days)
8) Docs, runbook, and SOC handoff (2 days)
acceptance_criteria: Policy Weave evaluates policies across a 1000-tenant test shard within the SLA (scan completes in configured window)
Automatic remediation executes for low-risk mismatches with idempotency checks and emits audit events
High-risk mismatches surface in Console with a one-click approval workflow and prevention of automatic changes
Evidence bundles are generated, signed, uploaded, and referenceable from a Console audit link
Telemetry: metrics for evaluations, remediations, failures, and mean time to remediate (MTTR) are emitted and visible in the compliance dashboard
End-to-end test: simulated region misassignment and shortened TTL produces correct status, remediation or approval flow, and evidence artifact
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for policy compiler and evaluator (coverage target 90%)
- Integration tests with Tenant Config Service using replayed snapshots
- Chaos test: introduce intermittent config read failures and ensure comparator retries and emits alerts
- Staging rollout to 50 tenants with monitoring of false positives and remediation rollbacks
- Run SOC tabletop with Security and Legal to validate evidence bundle acceptability
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Internal canary on infra and dev tenants (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Opt-in via Console for selected customers with compliance needs (4 weeks)
Phase 3: Default-on for new tenants and opt-in migration for legacy tenants (conditional on metrics)
Fallback: disable auto-remediation via tenant feature flag and run comparator in dry-run mode
